articles.author: Mahir Gündüz
articles.description:
## Why I Built Disk Mop
I've been using CCleaner for years, but after the Avast acquisition it became bloated and lost user trust. CleanMyMac is great but costs $40+/year and only works on Mac.
I wanted something modern, fast, cross-platform, and affordable. So I built it myself.
## What is Disk Mop?
Disk Mop is a desktop app for Windows and macOS that helps you clean, optimize, and analyze your disk space.
## Features
🧹 Browser Cache Cleaner — Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Safari
🔍 Duplicate File Finder — hash-based exact matching
🖼️ Visual Duplicate Finder — perceptual hash for similar photos
📊 Disk Treemap — interactive visualization of disk usage
📁 Large File Scanner — find space hogs instantly
📂 Empty Folder Finder — clean up clutter
🚀 Startup Manager — control what runs at boot
🔒 File Shredder — secure deletion (DoD 5220.22-M)
💾 Disk Health — SMART data monitoring
🧠 RAM Optimizer — free up memory
⚙️ Service Manager — manage background services
📋 Privacy Report — see what's tracking you
🗑️ Recycle Bin & Downloads Cleaner

🌐 DNS Cache Flush



## Tech Stack
Electron 31 + React 18 + Vite


TypeScript for type safety
Tailwind CSS v4 for styling
Zustand for state management
electron-updater for auto-updates
Custom IPC streaming for real-time progress events
## Architecture
The app follows a clean IPC pattern:
ipcMain.handle for request/response
webContents.send for streaming progress events
Preload bridge with contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld

Platform-specific code paths for Windows and macOS
## Pricing
Core features are completely free. PRO unlocks 20+ advanced tools for a one-time $19.90 — no subscriptions, no recurring fees.
## What's Next
Scheduled cleanup with Windows Task Scheduler
More languages (French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese)
Yearly pricing option
Linux support (maybe?)
## Try It Out
🔗 diskmop.com
I'd love to hear your feedback. What features would you want to see? Drop a comment below!
articles.title: I Built a Modern Disk Cleaner as a Solo Dev — Here's What I Learned

Most production RAG pipelines underperform for the same reason: the team treats retrieval as a solved vector-search problem, ships top-k embedding search, and then blames the generator when the answers are wrong. The "RAG is dead, long context replaces it" framing is the wrong fight. Long context doesn't fix retrieval — it hides retrieval failures behind a larger haystack while adding cost and latency.
This walkthrough is for engineers who already have a RAG prototype and want to know what to measure, what to fix, and in what order. By the end you'll have a minimal LangChain + FAISS + cross-encoder reranker pipeline and a clear separation between retrieval metrics and generation metrics.

TL;DR — I rebuilt my Next.js starter on Next 16 + React 19 with one rule: every default should be the one I'd pick on day 90, not day 1. This article walks through every load-bearing decision and the trap each one avoids.
